subject: Day 11: weight-check follow-up; settle the night-shift split
bodyText:
Today's focus
Day 11. Feeding is settling into a recognizable rhythm: feed, diaper, 60-90 minutes of sleep, repeat, around the clock. This is the week to make that rhythm sustainable for the adults, not just the baby.

Action items
- If the first-week weight check showed Avi below birth weight, confirm the recheck date the pediatrician asked for. AAP Bright Futures periodicity: https://www.aap.org/en/practice-management/bright-futures/bright-futures-tools-and-resources/
- Settle a night-shift split if both parents are home — one parent takes roughly 11pm-3am, the other 3am-7am. It beats both parents waking for everything.
- Reorder postpartum supplies that run short faster than expected: nipple cream, pads, burp cloths.
- If the SSN has not arrived yet, expect it 2-4 weeks post-birth; the 529 and the dependent tax claim both wait on it. SSA on getting a Social Security number: https://www.ssa.gov/ssnumber/
- Keep logging feeds and diaper output; six or more wet diapers a day is the reassuring floor.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Cord stump still attached and drying; evening fussiness building.
- [low concern] Witch's milk — a small breast-bud secretion from maternal hormone withdrawal — resolves in one to two weeks.
- [monitor] Persistent low mood, tearfulness, or anxiety in Anoushka beyond the normal baby-blues window.
- [call within 24h] Forceful projectile vomiting after most feeds. Fewer than six wet diapers in a day. Mother's foul-smelling discharge or fever.
- [call now] Rectal temperature at or above 100.4F (38.0C). Lethargy, refusing all feeds, blue or grey color, breathing faster than 60 per minute at rest, persistent grunting, projectile or bilious-green vomiting. Call 911 for blue lips or unresponsiveness!

Enrichment opportunities
- Accumulate 10-15 minutes of tummy time across the day; a rolled receiving blanket under the chest helps if he tires quickly. AAP HealthyChildren on tummy time: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx
- Respond to each of his coos and grunts as if he had spoken, pause, then respond again — conversational turns predict later language. Romeo et al., Psych Science 2018: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/
- Read aloud for five to ten minutes; adult material is fine, the rhythm of your voice is the active ingredient.
- During a calm-alert window, hold him close and let him study your face without competing stimulation.

Upcoming
- Day 14-21: first common growth spurt; cluster feeding for 24-48 hours.
- Day 14-21: target the EPDS maternal mood screen.
- Day 28-35: 1-month well visit window opens.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Quiets or turns toward a familiar voice
  AAP window: day 7-45
  What to look for: Voice recognition begins before birth; postnatally it shows as orienting or settling to a parent's voice.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-1-Month.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/recognizes-parent-voice/complete

- Watches your face when you talk
  AAP window: day 7-60
  What to look for: Baseline social orientation. Look for sustained gaze, even briefly, during alert windows.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/tracks-face-briefly/complete

- Moves both arms and both legs
  AAP window: day 0-60
  What to look for: Symmetric, spontaneous movement of all four limbs. Asymmetry warrants pediatric attention.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/moves-arms-and-legs/complete

- Reacts to loud sounds (startle, blink, stillness)
  AAP window: day 0-60
  What to look for: Confirms intact hearing response. Universal newborn hearing screen catches most cases but daily observation matters.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/responds-to-loud-sound/complete

- Brings hands within range of eyes and mouth
  AAP window: day 0-45
  What to look for: Early body awareness. Not yet purposeful — looks like accidental discovery.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-1-Month.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/brings-hands-near-face/complete
